Attackers can call /api/python/execute or /api/process/execute-async to run Python scripts and commands as the server user, even via malicious web pages abusing permissive CORS against loopback instances.

t: Cockpit CMS through 2.14.1 Stored XSS via Content Item Link Attributes
d: Cockpit CMS through 2.14.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users with content create or update permission to inject script via unescaped linked item _id values. Attackers can save an item whose link _id contains a double quote and HTML markup, executing script when administrators view the content dashboard or collection list.

t: Assimp through 6.0.6 Use-After-Free via OpenGEX Importer State Reuse
d: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a use-after-free and double free vulnerability in OpenGEXImporter.cpp because InternReadFile does not reset cached importer state between files. Attackers can supply OpenGEX files to applications reusing one Importer instance, causing freed node, camera, and material pointers to corrupt heap memory and crash.

t: Assimp through 6.0.6 Use-After-Free via BVH Loader Node List
d: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in BVHLoader.cpp that allows attackers to read freed aiNode objects because the mNodes vector is never cleared between files. Attackers can supply multiple BVH files to an application reusing one Importer instance, causing CreateAnimation to copy freed mName data into channel names, crashing the application or exposing heap contents.

t: Assimp through 6.0.6 Heap Out-of-Bounds Write via NaN Data in OBJ Exporter
d: Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the OBJ exporter that allows attackers to corrupt memory via NaN vertex components breaking comparator ordering. Attackers can supply a crafted PLY file with NaN texture coordinates or vertex colors that, when exported to OBJ in libc++ builds, writes file-controlled data past a heap buffer and crashes the application.

t: ex_aws_ses missing URI-encoding of list_name allows path injection into SES V2 request URLs
d: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_ses (ExAws.SES module) allows path injection into Amazon SES V2 request URLs. This vulnerability is associated with program file lib/ex_aws/ses.ex and program routines ExAws.SES.delete_contact_list/1, ExAws.SES.get_contact_list/1, ExAws.SES.update_contact_list/2, ExAws.SES.create_contact/3, ExAws.SES.get_contact/2, ExAws.SES.update_contact/3, ExAws.SES.delete_contact/2 and ExAws.SES.list_contacts/1. The V2 contact-list and contact functions interpolate the caller-supplied list_name into the request path without URI-encoding it, unlike the email address in the same functions which is passed through ExAws.Request.Url.uri_encode/1. An application that forwards untrusted input as a contact-list name lets an attacker embed /, .. or ? to escape the intended contact-lists/<name> path segment. A value such as x/../suppression/addresses/victim%40example.com makes a delete_contact_list/1 call arrive at the account-wide suppression list. The request is still signed with the application's own AWS credentials and sent to the configured SES host, so the impact is cross-resource request forgery inside the caller's own AWS account, not arbitrary SSRF. Applications that only use hardcoded or strictly validated list names are not affected. This issue affects ex_aws_ses: from 2.3.0 before 2.5.0.

t: TypiCMS Core before 17.0.46 API Token Disclosure via /api/users
d: TypiCMS Core before 17.0.46 contains an insufficiently protected credentials vulnerability that allows authenticated users with "read users" permission to view plaintext api_token values for all users, including superusers, via the GET /api/users endpoint. Attackers can steal a superuser's non-expiring, non-rotatable api_token from the JSON response and use it to gain full superuser API access, enabling creation and deletion of users, roles, and all content.

t: XML injection via unescaped tag keys and values in ex_aws_s3 object and bucket tagging
d: XML Injection vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows an attacker who controls tag keys or values to inject forged tag entries into S3 object and bucket tagging requests. ExAws.S3.put_object_tagging/4 and ExAws.S3.put_bucket_tagging/2 in lib/ex_aws/s3.ex build the <TagSet> request body by interpolating tag keys and values directly into <Key> and <Value> elements via to_string/1, without applying the module's existing escape_xml_string/1 helper (which delete_multiple_objects already uses for object keys). An application that forwards user-supplied data as a tag key or value lets an attacker close the intended element and inject attacker-chosen <Tag> entries. For example, a tag value of blue</Value></Tag><Tag><Key>owner</Key><Value>admin turns one intended tag into two tags on the wire. Because S3 honors tags in access-control conditions (aws:RequestTag, s3:ExistingObjectTag) and cost-allocation reporting, an injected tag can forge an authorization-relevant tag or corrupt the intended tag set. This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.2 before 2.6.0.

t: ex_aws_s3 XML injection in bucket-configuration builders
d: XML Injection vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 (ExAws.S3 module) allows an attacker to inject arbitrary XML configuration elements into S3 bucket-configuration request bodies via unescaped, caller-supplied values. This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/ex_aws/s3.ex and program routines ExAws.S3.put_bucket_logging/2, ExAws.S3.put_bucket_notification/2, ExAws.S3.put_bucket_replication/2, ExAws.S3.put_bucket_website/2. The bucket-configuration body builders construct their XML by interpolating caller-supplied values directly into the request body without escaping, and never route them through the module's own escape_xml_string/1 helper. A value containing XML metacharacters (<, >, &, quotes) can close the intended element early and open attacker-chosen elements, which the builder's trailing closing tag then closes, keeping the document single-rooted and well-formed. In a multi-tenant application where tenants configure their own bucket settings, an attacker who can influence one of the interpolated field values (for example the logging target, a notification ARN, a replication destination or Account, or a website redirect HostName) can inject arbitrary configuration nodes into a request the application signs and sends to AWS. The affected builders are reached through the public functions put_bucket_logging/2, put_bucket_notification/2, put_bucket_replication/2, and put_bucket_website/2. This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.5.9 before 2.6.0.

t: Copy-source header injection in ExAws.S3.upload_part_copy/8 via unencoded source key
d: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection') vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows HTTP header injection via an attacker-controlled copy-source key. ExAws.S3.upload_part_copy/8 in lib/ex_aws/s3.ex builds the x-amz-copy-source request header by interpolating the source bucket and object key directly into "/#{src_bucket}/#{src_object}" with no percent-encoding. The sibling function put_object_copy percent-encodes the bucket and each path segment before assembling the same header, but upload_part_copy skips encoding entirely. When the source key is derived from untrusted input, reserved characters (spaces, ?, &, =) pass through verbatim and corrupt the copy-source reference, so the copy targets the wrong object or fails. A key containing \r or \n can split or inject additional headers into the outgoing HTTP request, depending on how the configured HTTP backend serializes headers. Applications that pass a source bucket or object key derived from untrusted input to ExAws.S3.upload_part_copy/8 are affected. Applications that only ever pass trusted, well-formed keys are not affected. This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

t: XML injection in ExAws.S3.Utils.build_lifecycle_rule/1 in ex_aws_s3
d: ExAws.S3.Utils.build_lifecycle_rule/1 in ex_aws_s3 interpolates caller-supplied lifecycle rule fields (the rule id, filter prefix, tag key and value, storage class, and noncurrent-version count) directly into the PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration XML body without escaping XML metacharacters. An application that populates any of these fields from untrusted input (for example a tenant-supplied object tag) lets an attacker break out of the surrounding element and inject arbitrary XML into the request, including an entirely new lifecycle action such as a delete-after-one-day expiration that destroys the bucket's objects. The public entry point ExAws.S3.put_bucket_lifecycle/2 flows directly into this builder. This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.3.0 before 2.6.0.

t: XML injection via unescaped VersionId in ExAws.S3.delete_multiple_objects/3
d: XML Injection vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows an attacker who controls an object version id passed to ExAws.S3.delete_multiple_objects/3 to add objects to the batch delete. delete_multiple_objects/3 in lib/ex_aws/s3.ex builds the <Delete> request body by placing each object's version between <VersionId> tags without XML escaping. A version such as v1</VersionId></Object><Object><Key>important-file</Key></Object><Object><Key>x</Key><VersionId>v2 closes the caller's object and opens new ones, so S3 deletes objects the application never listed, including other users' objects in the same bucket. This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

t: S3 bucket name controls the host of presigned URLs in ex_aws_s3
d: Externally Controlled Reference to a Resource in Another Sphere vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows an attacker who controls an S3 bucket name to make presigned URLs and presigned POST forms point at a host of their choice. With virtual_host: true, s3_accelerate: true or bucket_as_host: true, ExAws.S3.presigned_url/5 and ExAws.S3.presigned_post/4 build the URL from the bucket name without checking it. A bucket such as attacker.example/x? turns the URL into https://attacker.example/x?.s3.amazonaws.com..., and the signature is computed for that host. Clients given the URL upload their files to, or download content from, the attacker's host, and every such URL discloses the access key id. With bucket_as_host: true any valid hostname works as the bucket name. This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

t: ExAws.S3 ACL grantee injection via unescaped grant headers in format_grant_header/1
d: ExAws.S3 constructs S3 ACL grant headers (such as x-amz-grant-read and x-amz-grant-full-control) in format_grant_header/1 by interpolating grantee identifiers into a quoted, comma-separated list without escaping. Grantee email and id values are wrapped in double quotes and joined with a comma, but double-quote, comma, and CR/LF characters in the value are not neutralized. An application that passes an attacker-influenced grantee value (for example an email address taken from a "share this object" feature) into an ACL grant option (grant_read, grant_write, grant_read_acp, grant_write_acp, or grant_full_control) lets the attacker close the quoted token and inject an additional grantee, such as the attacker's own canonical id or the predefined AllUsers group URI, into the header. S3 then applies the injected grantee, granting an arbitrary principal the same permission (up to full control or public access) in an unintended ACL grantee-injection and privilege-escalation issue. This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

t: Unvalidated object metadata in ex_aws_s3 enables HTTP header (CRLF) injection into S3 requests
d: ex_aws_s3 builds x-amz-meta-* request headers by interpolating user-supplied object metadata directly into header names and values without any validation. In ExAws.S3.Utils.build_meta_headers/1 (lib/ex_aws/s3/utils.ex), each :meta entry is turned into a header as {"x-amz-meta-#{k}", v} with no check for carriage return (CR), line feed (LF), or other illegal header bytes. Object metadata is routinely derived from end-user input (for example an upload service that lets users attach a comment or label to an object). When such input reaches ExAws.S3.put_object/4 or any other operation accepting the :meta option, a value containing CR/LF is carried unchanged into the outbound header list. If the configured HTTP adapter does not neutralize header values before writing them to the socket, the embedded CRLF starts a new header line, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary headers into (or split) the HTTP request the library sends to the S3 endpoint. This is an HTTP header (CRLF) injection leading to HTTP request splitting. The practical impact depends on the HTTP adapter, and no authentication is required beyond the ability to influence object metadata. This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

t: Code execution via the :log option of forged DBConnection.Stream structs in db_connection
d: Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code ('Unsafe Reflection') vulnerability in elixir-ecto db_connection allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code via a forged DBConnection.Stream or DBConnection.PrepareStream struct. The Enumerable implementations of both structs in lib/db_connection.ex run with the options stored in the struct. The :log option accepts a {module, function, arguments} tuple, which DBConnection applies. When code enumerates a forged struct, DBConnection calls the chosen function. This issue is not exploitable in db_connection alone. It is, in theory, a vulnerability of the downstream component. The root cause is a component that decodes untrusted input with :erlang.binary_to_term/2 and does not restrict which terms the result contains. The :safe option does not reject structs, and these structs contain only plain terms. Structs of other libraries can possibly lead to the same result, so a component that decodes untrusted terms stays at risk independently of db_connection. This record exists because the struct was used in attacks on such components. This issue affects db_connection: from 1.1.0 before 2.10.3.

t: Frappe LMS before 2.65.0 Missing Authorization via create_lms_certificate
d: Frappe LMS before 2.65.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows Batch Evaluators to modify any evaluation because the LMS Certificate Evaluation doctype lacks a has_permission scoping hook. Attackers can call the whitelisted create_lms_certificate method with any evaluation name to issue certificates for unassigned evaluations or learners outside their batches.

t: hping3 through commit 3547c76 Out-of-Bounds Write in display_ipopt() via Record Route
d: hping3 through commit 3547c76 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in display_ipopt() that allows remote attackers to overflow the static 40-byte old_rr buffer via a crafted IP Record Route option. Attackers acting as the probed host, on-path, or spoofing the target can send replies with option lengths up to 255 to hping3 running with -G/--rroute, corrupting global memory and crashing hping3.

t: Pangolin before 1.21.0 Authentication Bypass via URL-Encoded Slashes in Path Rules
d: Pangolin before 1.21.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in isPathAllowed() in server/lib/pathMatch.ts that splits paths on literal slashes without percent-decoding or resolving dot segments. Unauthenticated remote attackers can send paths with encoded slashes and dot segments to match public bypass rules while backends serve protected paths.

t: NocoDB before 2026.10.2 Session Revocation DoS via Password Reset Request
d: NocoDB before 2026.10.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in passwordForgot() that allows unauthenticated attackers to revoke a user's sessions by requesting a password reset. Attackers who know a user's email can repeatedly request resets to sign out users, including super-admins, and permanently destroy their OAuth and MCP application authorizations.

t: Pyro through 1.9.2 Insecure Deserialization RCE via ParamStoreDict.load()
d: Pyro through 1.9.2 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability in ParamStoreDict.load() that calls torch.load with weights_only=False, unpickling arbitrary Python objects. Attackers can trick users into loading a crafted parameter file defining __reduce__ to execute code with the privileges of the Python process.

t: fastcore through 2.2.44 Path Traversal via untar_dir Tar Extraction
d: fastcore through 2.2.44 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the fastcore.xtras.untar_dir() archive extraction helper that allows attackers who supply a crafted tar archive to write files outside the intended extraction directory. The internal _unpack() function passes the archive to shutil.unpack_archive() without a tar extraction filter, member path validation, or a containment check, so archive members with absolute paths or ../ traversal sequences are written to arbitrary locations writable by the application process when running on Python versions before 3.14. Applications that extract untrusted archives with untar_dir() can have application files, configuration, or importable code overwritten, which can lead to code execution, data modification, or denial of service.

t: Valkey JSON: Use-after-free in array mutation commands through a recursive JSONPath
d: In Valkey JSON 1.0.0 through 1.0.2, a recursive JSONPath expression such as $..* returns both an array and elements nested inside it. The size-changing mutators (JSON.ARRAPPEND, JSON.ARRINSERT, JSON.ARRPOP, JSON.ARRTRIM and JSON.CLEAR) process the ancestor first, which can reallocate its element buffer and free the old storage while the descendant entries in the result set still point into it; the module then writes through those dangling pointers. An authenticated user who can run these commands can use this to reliably crash the server, and it has been developed into remote code execution as the user the server runs as. Servers that do not load the JSON module, including through valkey-bundle, are not affected.

t: Valkey: Use-after-free in the RDMA transport when a client is freed while pending data is processed
d: In Valkey 8.0.x before 8.0.11, 8.1.x before 8.1.10, 9.0.x before 9.0.6 and 9.1.x before 9.1.2, the RDMA transport's pending-data handler walks its connection list with an iterator that caches the next entry. A command processed from inside that loop, such as CLIENT KILL, can synchronously free another client's connection, and closing an RDMA connection did not remove it from the pending list, so the handler then uses freed memory. An authenticated user can use this to reliably crash the server, and the freed heap chunk can be reclaimed with attacker-influenced bytes. Only servers built with RDMA support (USE_RDMA) and configured with an RDMA listener are affected.

t: Valkey: Integer truncation in cluster publish message construction causes a heap buffer overflow
d: In Valkey before 7.2.15, 8.0.x before 8.0.12, 8.1.x before 8.1.11, 9.0.x before 9.0.7, 9.1.x before 9.1.3 and 9.2.0-rc1, running in cluster mode, clusterCreatePublishMsgBlock computes the length of the cluster bus message for a PUBLISH or SPUBLISH as a size_t but passes it to createClusterMsgSendBlock as a uint32_t. When the channel and message together exceed 4 GiB, the length is truncated, a buffer far smaller than the message is allocated, and the full channel and message are then copied into it. An authenticated user who can publish, for example by building the arguments in a script, can overflow the heap with attacker-controlled bytes. This reliably crashes the server and may lead to remote code execution. Servers that do not run in cluster mode are not affected.

t: Valkey: Use-after-free of the Lua interpreter state through the script debugger's command cache
d: In Valkey 9.1.0 and 9.1.1, the Lua script debugger builds its command table once and caches it with a pointer to the Lua interpreter state that was current at the time. SCRIPT FLUSH ASYNC recreates the scripting engine and frees the previous interpreter state without invalidating that cache, so the next debugger command dereferences freed memory. An authenticated user who can run scripting commands can use this to reliably crash the server, and by reclaiming the freed heap chunk with attacker-controlled bytes can escalate it to control of an indirect call, which may lead to remote code execution. The fix also addresses a second use-after-free in ldbLogStackValue. Valkey 8.0.x and 8.1.x use the previous debugger and are not affected.

t: Valkey: Use-after-free when client eviction frees the client whose command is still executing
d: In Valkey before 7.2.16, 8.0.x before 8.0.13, 8.1.x before 8.1.12, 9.0.x before 9.0.8, 9.1.x before 9.1.4 and 9.2.0 release candidates, when client eviction is enabled (maxmemory-clients is not 0), an authenticated user who can write to a key that other clients are blocked on (for example with BLPOP, BLMPOP, BZPOPMIN or XREAD BLOCK) can trigger a use-after-free. While the clients blocked on that key are served, evictClients() can select and free the client whose command made the key ready, although that command is still executing, and the server then keeps using the freed client. The blocked clients do not have to belong to the attacker. The result is a reliable crash of the server process. Servers with the default maxmemory-clients 0 are not affected.

Server-Side Request Forgery in the SSO SAML configuration feature of the TXOne StellarOne web console allows an authenticated administrator to issue server-side requests to arbitrary destinations, including internal services. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

t: Prevent Direct Access before 2.8.9.2 Information Disclosure via robots.txt
d: Prevent Direct Access – Protect WordPress Files plugin before 2.8.9.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain protected file names and paths by requesting the dynamically generated robots.txt file, which appends Disallow rules containing attachment page URLs and direct _pda/ directory file paths for all protected media. Attackers can send an unauthenticated HTTP request to robots.txt to enumerate original file names, upload directory structures, and attachment slugs, undermining the plugin's file protection and potentially enabling direct file access if server-level restrictions are misconfigured or absent.
r: Prevent Direct Access – Protect WordPress Files

d: Missing server-side authorization in the IPC interface of TXOne StellarProtect and Stellar Agent (Windows) allows a local attacker to issue privileged commands without credentials. This issue affects StellarProtect: 3.3 and earlier; Stellar Agent (Windows): before 5.0.3056. *Note: Stellar Agent (Windows) is the new name for StellarProtect.

Unverified configuration export destination path in TXOne StellarProtect and Stellar Agent (Windows) allows a local attacker to export the product configuration to an arbitrary directory with SYSTEM privileges. This issue affects StellarProtect: 3.3 and earlier; Stellar Agent (Windows): before 5.0.3056. *Note: Stellar Agent (Windows) is the new name for StellarProtect.

t: Unauthenticated remote code execution through struct values in Erlang term request bodies
d: Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in the application/vnd.hex+erlang request body parser in hexpm hexpm allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute operating system commands via a crafted Erlang external term format request body. This vulnerability was actively exploited against the hex.pm service on 2026-11-23. HexpmWeb.ErlangFormat.decode/1 in lib/hexpm_web/erlang_format.ex decodes the body with Plug.Crypto.non_executable_binary_to_term/2, which accepts maps that have a __struct__ key. HexpmWeb.PlugParser.parse/5 returns the decoded term as the request params. The parser runs in the endpoint before routing and authentication, so a POST to any route reaches it. Elixir dispatches protocols on the __struct__ key, so the client selects which Inspect and Enumerable implementations run when error reporting inspects the params. A chain through Ecto.Query.DynamicExpr and DBConnection.Stream reaches an apply/3 call on a {module, function, args} tuple taken from the request body. This issue affects hex.pm: from 2016-02-23 before 2026-11-23; hexpm/hexpm: from ab1bbcef7cc8395d1056d3b1aa6a174353492d59 before 379b0a29bcc95164249f38ad7d772a37a8ff9533.

Improper access control of a file path in TXOne StellarProtect and Stellar Agent (Windows) allows a local attacker to write or overwrite arbitrary files with SYSTEM privileges. This issue affects StellarProtect: 3.3 and earlier; Stellar Agent (Windows): before 5.0.3056. *Note: Stellar Agent (Windows) is the new name for StellarProtect.

t: Ash.Type.Keyword casts client input as trusted stored data, bypassing the input validation of its field types
d: Improper Input Validation vulnerability in ash-project ash allows an attacker to bypass the input validation of the field types of a :keyword attribute or argument. Ash.Type.Keyword.cast_input/2 in lib/ash/type/keyword.ex converts a map input to a keyword list in try_map_to_keyword/2, which casts each declared field with Ash.Type.cast_stored/3. That function is meant for trusted values read back from the data layer, so client input skips the cast_input/2 of each field type. apply_constraints/2 casts the result again with cast_input/2, but most types accept a value of their own type unchanged. An embedded resource field is built without its create action, so its validations and changes do not run and its non-public attributes can be set. A :function field accepts a capture string such as &Mod.fun/1, and a :term field decodes Erlang external term format. This issue affects ash: from 3.24.0 before 3.38.1.

t: Unbounded Converter Memoisation in twig/markdown-extra Keyed on Template-Controlled Options
d: The html_to_markdown filter of twig/markdown-extra keeps an HtmlConverter for each distinct mapping of options it receives. They're kept in a static array, with no size limit and no eviction. The options are an argument of the filter. A template that passes options taken from the input, or a sandboxed template, can therefore make this cache grow without limit. The cache outlives the environment, so it fills the memory of long-running workers. The cache now keeps at most 100 converters, like the formatter caches of IntlExtension.

t: Sandbox Tag Allow-List Bypass via the Branch of a `guard` Tag That Isn't Selected
d: The guard tag compiles only one of its branches, depending on whether a callable exists. The other branch was still parsed, though. The extends, use, macro and block tags in it registered their effects on the template. The sandbox doesn't see these tags, since that branch isn't compiled. A sandboxed template allowed to use guard could therefore extend a template, import blocks and define macros, while the policy doesn't allow these tags: {% guard filter upper %}{% else %}{% extends "parent.html" %}{% endguard %} The templates reached this way come from the loader of the sandbox, and they are sandboxed too. What the branch that isn't selected registers on the parser is now discarded.

t: Missing autoescaping for a variable named like a macro import alias of another scope
d: The escaper considered x.attr, x['key'] and x.method() safe whenever {% import ... as x %} appeared anywhere in the template. Macro calls haven't needed this rule since Twig 3.0. It only matched ordinary variables that have the name of an alias imported in another block or macro, and printed them without escaping: {% block header %}{% import _self as item %}{{ item.hello() }}{% endblock %} {% block content %}{% for item in items %}{{ item.body }}{% endfor %}{% endblock %} Here, item.body is printed raw. This leads to XSS when the value comes from an attacker. The same happens with an import in a macro and an argument of the same name in another macro. It also happens with a template-level import placed after the block that uses the name. The rule is removed. Macro calls through an alias are still considered safe.

t: Sandboxed templates can rewrite application-owned `Markup` objects through their constructor
d: The sandbox allows every method of Twig\Markup objects, including their public constructor. A sandboxed template can therefore call __construct() on any Markup object that it reaches, and replace its content: {% do banner.__construct('<script>alert(1)</script>', 'UTF-8') %} A template gains nothing by rewriting its own output. The impact is on the Markup objects that come from the application and are also rendered elsewhere, like a global in a long-running worker. Their new content then ends up in trusted pages that aren't sandboxed. The sandbox no longer allows calling the constructor of Markup objects.

t: Sandbox property allow-list bypass via `html_cva()` variant values
d: Cva::apply() converted the values of variants, default variants and compound variants with (array). These values come from the arguments of html_cva(). A sandboxed template could therefore pass any object of its context, and print the private and protected properties of that object: {{ html_cva('base', {c: {p: user}}).apply({c: 'p'}) }} Variant maps that are ArrayAccess objects were also read with a key that the template chooses, without the property check of the sandbox. The template then printed the offsets that the object returned. Applications are affected when the sandbox allows the html_cva function and the apply method of Twig\Extra\Html\Cva. A value that isn't an array is now treated as a single item, so objects are dropped and never match a variant. Variant maps are also only used when they're arrays.

t: Sandbox property allow-list bypass via the `join` filter on non-iterable objects
d: The join filter converted a value that isn't iterable with (array) $value. For an object, that gives every property, including the private and protected ones. A sandboxed template allowed to use join could therefore print properties that the policy denies, and that templates can't read otherwise: {{ user|join(',') }} A value that isn't iterable is now joined as a single item. A Stringable object prints its checked string, and other objects throw, as with the first and last filters.

t: Sandbox allow-list and `__toString()` bypass via a dynamic `embed` parent expression
d: When the parent of an embed tag was an expression other than a string or a variable, the sandbox didn't see that expression. The functions, filters and tests of the expression weren't checked against the policy, and neither were its conversions to strings. A sandboxed template allowed to use embed could therefore call any function, filter or test, and any __toString() method: {% embed 'leak_' ~ app_secret() %}{% endembed %} Method calls and property reads were not affected, since they're checked at runtime. The sandbox now checks the parent expression of embed like any other expression of the template.

t: Sandbox `__toString()` policy bypass via spread arguments
d: Since Twig 3.28.0, the sandbox skips the toString() check of an argument whose PHP parameter can't hold a string, like an int. A spread argument was mapped to a single parameter, although it fills every parameter from its position on. A sandboxed template could therefore call a denied toString() method: {{ tag(...[1, obj]) }} Here, the first parameter of tag() is an int, and a later one accepts strings. Applications are affected when they allow such a function, filter or test in the sandbox. No built-in callable is affected. A spread argument is now checked unless every parameter that it can fill has a safe type.

t: Sandbox `__toString()` policy bypass via assignment and destructuring expressions
d: The sandbox checks that a template may call toString() on an object before converting it to a string. Since Twig 3.23.0, assignments like x = obj, and the destructuring forms [a] = list and {a} = obj, evaluate to the value that they assign. The sandbox didn't check that value, so a sandboxed template could call a denied toString() method: {{ (x = obj) }} {{ ({secret: s} = obj)|join }} No tag needs to be allowed. The sandbox now checks the result of assignments like the result of filters and functions. {% do x = obj %} and {% if (x = obj) %} still work, since they don't convert the value to a string.

t: Sandbox `__toString()` policy bypass via the input of custom tests
d: The sandbox checks that a template may call toString() on an object before converting it to a string. It didn't check the input of tests. The PHP callable of a test may convert this input to a string, for example when its parameter is typed as string. PHP then calls toString() on an object without the sandbox checking it first: {{ obj is upperish }} Applications are affected when they register such a test and allow it in the sandbox. No built-in test is affected. The sandbox now checks the input of tests like the input of filters. The built-in tests that never convert their input to a string still skip the check.

t: Sandbox `__toString()` policy bypass via the `is true` test
d: The sandbox checks that a template may call toString() on an object before converting it to a string. For an object, the is true test evaluates to the object itself, and that result wasn't checked. A sandboxed template could therefore print an object through a denied toString() method: {{ obj is true }} The same applies when the result is concatenated or passed to a filter. No tag needs to be allowed. A test in a boolean context, like {% if obj is true %}, isn't affected, since it doesn't convert the object to a string. The sandbox now checks the result of tests like the result of filters and functions.

t: Type confusion via structural idempotency guard in ExAws.Dynamo.Encoder.encode/2
d: Improper Validation of Specified Type of Input in ExAws.Dynamo.Encoder.encode/2 in ex_aws_dynamo allows an attacker who controls map data passed into a DynamoDB call to choose the raw stored DynamoDB AttributeValue. The encode/2 function in lib/ex_aws/dynamo/encoder.ex has one clause per DynamoDB type descriptor ("S", "N", "B", "BOOL", "M", "L", "NS", "SS", "BS", "NULL") that treats any map merely containing such a key as already encoded and returns it verbatim, bypassing the ExAws.Dynamo.Encodable protocol. The match is on the presence of the key alone, so no check is made that the value is well formed for the claimed type, and extra keys and arbitrary nested content survive untouched. An application that threads user-influenced map data (a decoded JSON body, a nested attribute, or an expression_attribute_values entry) into a Dynamo write or query therefore lets the user, rather than the application, decide the stored attribute's declared type, its bytes, and its structure. This type confusion breaks round-trip integrity and enables silent persistent data corruption, injection of attributes and raw binaries the schema never sanctioned, subversion of application authorization checks that trust the decoded type of a value, and a decoder crash on read-back that denies reads of the affected item to other users of the same table. This issue affects ex_aws_dynamo: from 2.0.0 before 4.3.0.

t: ex_aws_kms defaults RSA key-material wrapping to PKCS#1 v1.5 in get_parameters_for_import/3
d: Use of RSA Algorithm without OAEP vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_kms (ExAws.KMS module) causes callers who import external key material to wrap their secret KMS key material with the deprecated PKCS#1 v1.5 padding scheme by default. This vulnerability is associated with program file lib/ex_aws/kms.ex and program routine ExAws.KMS.get_parameters_for_import/3. ExAws.KMS.get_parameters_for_import/3 defaults its wrapping_algorithm argument to "RSAES_PKCS1_V1_5". AWS KMS returns this value as the WrappingAlgorithm for the import operation, and it dictates the RSA padding scheme the caller uses to wrap (RSA-encrypt) their secret key material before calling ImportKeyMaterial. AWS KMS also supports the stronger RSAES_OAEP_SHA_1 and RSAES_OAEP_SHA_256 schemes. By defaulting to RSAES_PKCS1_V1_5, the library steers callers who do not explicitly override the argument toward the weakest of the three. PKCS#1 v1.5 encryption padding is susceptible to Bleichenbacher adaptive chosen-ciphertext (padding oracle) attacks, which can recover the wrapped plaintext without the private key given an oracle that reveals whether a decrypted value was validly padded. Because the unwrap happens inside AWS KMS, which does not expose a padding oracle, the practical exploitability is low and this is a defense-in-depth weakness. Callers can avoid the weak default by explicitly passing "RSAES_OAEP_SHA_256" (or "RSAES_OAEP_SHA_1") as the wrapping algorithm. This issue affects ex_aws_kms: from 2.1.0 before 2.7.0.

t: S3 bucket name controls the request host in ex_aws virtual-host requests
d: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws allows an attacker who controls an S3 bucket name to send the application's signed S3 requests to a host of their choice. With virtual_host: true, ExAws.Operation.S3.add_bucket_to_path/2 in lib/ex_aws/operation/s3.ex builds the request hostname from the bucket name and the configured host without checking the bucket name. A bucket such as attacker.example/x? turns the request URL into https://attacker.example/x?.s3.amazonaws.com/key, so the request is signed for and sent to attacker.example. The attacker receives upload bodies, the access key id and request signature, and any STS session token, and controls the response the application parses. With bucket_as_host: true the bucket is the whole hostname, so any valid hostname redirects the request. This issue affects ex_aws: from 2.1.7 before 2.8.0.

t: ex_aws normalizes .. in S3 object keys client-side, allowing bucket or key-prefix escape
d: Relative path traversal in ex_aws allows an attacker who controls an S3 object key to escape the intended bucket or key prefix. When ex_aws builds a path-style S3 request, ExAws.Operation.S3.add_bucket_to_path/2 in lib/ex_aws/operation/s3.ex joins the bucket name and the object key into a single path string and then normalizes it, collapsing . and .. segments the way a filesystem path would. Because the bucket is the first segment of the combined string, a leading ../ in the object key pops the bucket off the path. With bucket mybucket and a key of ../victim/secret.txt, the combined /mybucket/../victim/secret.txt normalizes to /victim/secret.txt, so the request (signed with the application's own credentials) is sent to bucket victim. The same mechanism collapses ../ within a key, defeating any isolation an application enforces by prepending a trusted prefix. Only the default path-style configuration is affected; requests built with virtual_host: true do not run this normalization. Because S3 treats object keys as opaque and does not resolve .. itself, the client-side normalization introduces a traversal that would not otherwise exist. Any application that derives an S3 object key from untrusted input and relies on the bucket, or a key prefix, as a tenant or trust boundary is exposed to cross-bucket or cross-prefix read and write, depending on the operation and the credentials' permissions. This issue affects ex_aws: from 2.1.7 before 2.8.0.

t: IMDSv2 metadata token request follows HTTP redirects in ex_aws
d: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in ex_aws (instance metadata token provider). This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/ex_aws/instance_meta_token_provider.ex and program routines ExAws.InstanceMetaTokenProvider.request_token/1 and ExAws.InstanceMetaTokenProvider.get/1. ex_aws requests its IMDSv2 session token from the link-local metadata endpoint (http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token) with HTTP redirect following enabled. Because the token request follows 3xx redirects and does not restrict the redirect target to the link-local range, an attacker who can influence the response to the metadata request (for example an on-segment neighbor spoofing the link-local address) can answer with a redirect to an arbitrary host. The library follows the redirect and accepts the arbitrary host's response body as the IMDSv2 session token, caching it and sending it as the x-aws-ec2-metadata-token header on every subsequent metadata and credential request. This issue affects ex_aws: from 2.3.0 before 2.8.0.

t: Apache BuildStream: symlink following via plugin API
d: UNIX symbolic link (symlink) following vulnerability in Apache BuildStream allows source plugins to inadvertently read or write files on the host, with the privileges of the user running BuildStream, via symlinks from malicious or compromised source archives or respositories, as part of source fetching. The impact of this issue is mitigated by: * BuildStream projects should only use trusted sources in their elements as otherwise the build output can also not be trusted * None of the source plugins in the buildstream, buildstream-plugins or buildstream-plugins-community repositories use the vulnerable `open_file` method This issue affects Apache BuildStream: through 2.8.1. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.8.2, which fixes the issue.

t: Apache BuildStream: path traversal via unvalidated CAS Directory
d: Improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory ('path traversal') vulnerability in Apache BuildStream allows malicious or compromised artifact or execution servers to write files on the host, with the privileges of the user running BuildStream, as part of `bst artifact checkout`. The impact of this issue is mitigated by: * BuildStream projects should only use trusted servers for remote cache and remote execution as otherwise the build output can also not be trusted This issue affects Apache BuildStream: through 2.8.1. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.8.2, which fixes the issue.

t: S3 object key query-string injection and truncation via unencoded reserved characters in ex_aws
d: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output vulnerability in ex_aws (S3 request URL construction). This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/ex_aws/request/url.ex and program routines ExAws.Request.Url.build/2, ExAws.Request.Url.sanitize/2 and ExAws.Request.Url.get_path/2. ex_aws does not percent-encode reserved characters in S3 object keys when it assembles the request URL. A literal ? in an object key survives unencoded: build/2 inserts the operation path verbatim and URI.to_string/1 emits it without encoding, and sanitize/2 then splits the flattened URL on the first ?, treating everything after it as the query string. Because the split runs before uri_encode is applied to the path, the ? is never neutralized, and the recovered query is re-inserted without any encoding. An attacker who controls part of an object key (for example a download or upload keyed by a user-supplied filename) can therefore truncate the key past application-appended suffixes, causing the request to address a different object than the application intended, and can inject live S3 sub-resource operations (such as ?acl, ?tagging or ?versions) into the request. The manipulated URL is signed and transmitted normally, so the tampering is authorized like any legitimate request. This issue affects ex_aws: from 2.1.2 before 2.8.0.

t: SQL Injection in ITG Computer's vSRM
d: Improper neutralization of special elements used in an SQL command ('SQL injection') vulnerability in ITG Bilgisayar Teknoloji Grubu Tic. Ltd. Şti. VSRM allows SQL Injection. This issue affects vSRM: from v14.08.3 before v14.08.5.

t: Apache IoTDB MCP Server: Connection password logged during startup in iotdb-mcp-server
d: Apache IoTDB MCP Server logs the IoTDB connection password in plaintext during startup, allowing anyone with access to the logs to obtain the credential. This issue affects Apache IoTDB MCP Server: through 0.2.0. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.3.0, which fixes the issue.

t: IDOR in ITG Computer's vSRM
d: Authorization bypass through User-Controlled key vulnerability in ITG Bilgisayar Teknoloji Grubu Tic. Ltd. Şti. VSRM allows Accessing Functionality Not Properly Constrained by ACLs. This issue affects vSRM: from v14.08.3 before v14.08.5.
v: ITG Bilgisayar Teknoloji Grubu Tic. Ltd. Şti.

t: Authenticated heap buffer overflow in rms_mqtt
d: A heap buffer overflow issue exists in the rms_mqtt daemon on Teltonika Networks devices. An authenticated attacker with access to the affected service could trigger a heap-based buffer overflow, resulting in a denial of service. This issue affects RUT: from 7.0 through 7.18.0; RUTX: from 7.0 through 7.18.0; RUTM: from 7.0 through 7.18.0; RUTC: from 7.0 through 7.18.0; ATRM: from 7.16.1 through 7.18.0; TRB: from 7.0 through 7.18.0; OTD: from 7.11.1 through 7.18.0; TAP: from 7.4.3 through 7.18.0; DAP: from 7.12 through 7.18.0; SWM: from 1.6.3 through 1.7.1; TSW: from 1.1 through 1.7.1.

t: Apache Allura: XSS in ticket tracker
d: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS) vulnerability in Apache Allura's ticket tracking tool. This issue affects Apache Allura: before 1.23.0. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.23.0, which fixes the issue.

t: Apache Pinot: Controller local file disclosure during URI ingestion
d: In Apache Pinot 0.7.1 through 1.5.1, a caller who can submit URI ingestion jobs can select local files readable by the controller process. If the file can be ingested using the destination table’s schema and input format, users with query access to that table can read its contents. Upgrade to Apache Pinot 1.6.0 and keep controller.ingestFromURI.allowLocalFileSystem at its default value of false on every controller. Until you can upgrade, block the URI ingestion endpoint if it is unused or restrict it to trusted operators.

t: Unbounded Out-of-Order Fragment Reassembly in QUIC Streams
d: Issue summary: A QUIC peer that sends many small out-of-order STREAM fragments while withholding the first byte of the stream may cause OpenSSL to buffer a large number of reassembly nodes occupying much larger memory than the actual data sent. Impact summary: A remote peer can pin large amounts of memory on a server that accepts incoming QUIC streams, potentially exhausting memory and causing Denial of Service. CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling Description: QUIC receive flow control limits the highest byte offset a peer may reach on a stream. It does not limit how many out-of-order fragments the receiver buffers. OpenSSL allocates a reassembly node for each non-adjacent STREAM fragment and never caps the count. A peer that opens a stream and sends many one-byte fragments at increasing offsets, while withholding the first byte, makes the receiver retain one node per fragment without delivering any data. Only applications that accept incoming streams are exposed. With the default policy, which rejects peer-initiated streams, the stream is torn down before state accumulates. Because the read side never advances past the missing prefix, the flow control window never slides and the nodes stay pinned for the life of the connection. The per-stream window bounds the highest offset, so the memory one stream can pin is finite, but it can reach tens of megabytes and, across many streams and connections, drive memory pressure and Denial of Service. The severity is limited because the exhaustion is bounded by flow control and requires a non-default configuration. FIPS impact: no The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

t: Management System Authentication Bypass in ITG Computer's vSRM
d: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password vulnerability in ITG Bilgisayar Teknoloji Grubu Tic. Ltd. Şti. VSRM allows Password Recovery Exploitation. This issue affects vSRM: from v14.08.3 before v14.08.5.

t: Unauthenticated Stored XSS via File Upload in ITG Computer Technologies's vSRM

t: Apache Jena: Improper input validation in SPARQL expressions can lead to excessive CPU/memory usage
d: Improper input validation in some SPARQL functions available in Apache Jena ARQ allows users to submit SPARQL queries that cause excessive CPU and/or memory usage. This may be the result of intentionally malicious inputs in the query itself, or an expression applied over data that has been insufficiently validated/sanitised Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.3.0, which fixes this issue.

t: File Upload Extension Filter Bypass via Trailing Dot in ITG Computer Technologies's vSRM
d: Unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability in ITG Bilgisayar Teknolojileri Grubu Ltd. Şti. VSRM allows Using Malicious Files. This issue affects vSRM: from v14.08.1 before v14.08.5.
v: ITG Bilgisayar Teknolojileri Grubu Ltd. Şti.

t: Unauthenticated Stored XSS via File Upload in ITG Computer Technologies's vSRM
d: Improper neutralization of input during web page generation ('cross-site scripting') vulnerability in ITG Bilgisayar Teknolojileri Grubu Ltd. Şti. VSRM allows XSS Through HTTP Headers. This issue affects vSRM: from v14.08.1 before v14.08.5.
v: ITG Bilgisayar Teknolojileri Grubu Ltd. Şti.

t: Apache Jena: SPARQL Property Path optimisation can lead to excessive memory consumption.
d: A Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability exists in the ARQ SPARQL Query Optimiser in Apache Jena ARQ prior to version 6.3.0 that allows a SPARQL query to use that cause excessive memory usage. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.3.0, which fixes this issue. Users who are unable to upgrade immediately, especially those who operate a public facing SPARQL service/application backed by Apache Jena are recommended to configure the ARQ symbol arq:optPathFlatten=false in their SPARQL execution context which disables the problematic optimisation.

t: SUSE Neuvector memory-safety issues in dataplane could lead to DoS
d: Various memory-safety issues in dataplane of SUSE Neuvector before 5.5, 5.5.0 before 5.5.6, 5.6.0 before 5.6.5 could be used by remote attackers to trigger crashes.

t: Apache Texera: Users can export results from workflows for which they do not otherwise have permissions for
d: Missing authorization in the workflow export service of Apache Texera allows a logged-in user to potentially read the result of a workflow for which they do not otherwise have permission for This issue affects Apache Texera: from 1.1.0-incubating before 1.3.0-incubating. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0-incubating, which fixes the issue

t: Multiple Vulnerabilities in GlobalEduca's Job Portal
d: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in 'activity[description]' field in the POST request to '/people/{person_id}/cvs/{cv_id}/activities' on the job portal. The server stores the data entered by an authenticated candidate and displays it in the recruitment interface without sanitizing it. When reviewing an application, the recruiter’s browser can execute the injected JavaScript code within the context of their session on the portal.

t: Apache Texera: Missing authorization when the workflow compiling service resolves operator file paths
d: Missing authorization in the workflow compiling service of Apache Texera allows a logged-in user to read the column names of datasets they have not been given access to, and the header line of files on the host that runs the service. This issue affects Apache Texera: from 1.1.0-incubating before 1.3.0-incubating. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0-incubating, which fixes the issue

t: Apache Texera: Missing authorization when adding public projects
d: Missing Authorization vulnerability in the public project REST API of Apache Texera (incubating). The public project API did not check that a project had been made public before granting the caller read access to it. Any authenticated user with an approved account (the REGULAR or ADMIN role; new accounts need administrator approval by default) could give themselves lasting read access to other users' private projects and to the private workflows in them, including their version and execution history. Only deployments in which users have created projects are affected; the project feature is hidden in the web UI by default. This issue affects Apache Texera: from 1.1.0-incubating before 1.3.0-incubating. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0-incubating, which fixes the issue by removing the deprecated project feature and its data. If you cannot upgrade immediately, configure the reverse proxy in front of Texera to reject every request whose path starts with /api/project, /api/public/project or /api/access/project, and every request whose path contains ';', which the Texera server ignores when routing. Respond with 403 or 404, not 401: from 1.2.0-incubating the web UI treats a 401 as an expired session, and the workflow pages request the project list when they load. Unless an administrator has enabled the project feature, this does not affect other functionality; those project-list requests are simply rejected. Make sure the Texera server is reachable only through that proxy. Blocking and upgrading do not undo access obtained earlier. Before upgrading, review the project_user_access table, which remains empty unless someone has used the feature: treat any READ grant on a project that is not listed in public_project, and that the project's owner did not give, as suspect. The upgrade deletes this table. Removing a grant does not remove copies the user may already have made of the workflows.

t: Apache Texera: Missing authorization in the project API
d: Missing Authorization vulnerability in the project REST API of Apache Texera (incubating). The project API did not check that the caller owns, or has been granted access to, the project being accessed. Any authenticated user with an approved account (the REGULAR or ADMIN role; new accounts need administrator approval by default) could view, modify or delete other users' projects, change which workflows those projects contain, and see the e-mail addresses of a project's owner and collaborators. The project feature is hidden in the web UI by default, but the API was reachable regardless of that setting. This issue affects Apache Texera: from 1.1.0-incubating before 1.3.0-incubating. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0-incubating, which fixes the issue by removing the deprecated project feature and its data. If you cannot upgrade immediately, configure the reverse proxy in front of Texera to reject every request whose path starts with /api/project, /api/public/project or /api/access/project, and every request whose path contains ';', which the Texera server ignores when routing. Respond with 403 or 404, not 401: from 1.2.0-incubating the web UI treats a 401 as an expired session, and the workflow pages request the project list when they load. Unless an administrator has enabled the project feature, this does not affect other functionality; those project-list requests are simply rejected. Make sure the Texera server is reachable only through that proxy. Blocking and upgrading do not undo access obtained earlier. Before upgrading, review the project, project_user_access and workflow_of_project tables, which remain empty unless someone has used the feature, and remove rows you do not expect; the upgrade deletes these tables. Do not copy project grants into workflow_user_access without checking each one.

t: Apache Texera: Missing authorization on the computing unit workflow websocket
d: Missing Authorization vulnerability in the computing unit workflow websocket of Apache Texera (incubating) allows an authenticated user to view workflow results, control workflow executions, and run code in a computing unit they have not been granted. In local JVM and single-node Docker Compose deployments this is possible directly; in Kubernetes deployments it is possible from code running inside another computing unit in the cluster. This issue affects Apache Texera : from 1.1.0 through 1.2.0. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0, which fixes the issue. Local JVM and Docker Compose deployments do not provide the full security model and should only be used by trusted users.

t: Apache Texera: The DELETE /api/quota/deleteCollection/{eid} endpoint does not require authentication, allowing an unauthenticated user to delete workflow execut
d: An API which can allow a user to delete any workflow execution results is missing authentication. This means that any workflow result could be deleted by someone able to reach the Texera instance. This issue affects Apache Texera: from 1.1.0-incubating before 1.3.0-incubating. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0-incubating, which fixes the issue.

t: Apache Texera: Missing authentication on the Python virtual environment endpoints in non-Kubernetes deployments
d: Missing Authentication for Critical Function in Apache Texera (incubating). The Python virtual environment (PVE) management endpoints of a computing unit are not authenticated by the application itself. In the local JVM and single-node Docker Compose deployments, which place no authenticating gateway in front of the services, these endpoints are reachable without credentials. The Kubernetes deployment gates them at the gateway, so only the Kubernetes deployment provides the full security model described in SECURITY.md. This issue affects Apache Texera (incubating): from 1.1.0 through 1.2.0. Users are recommended to use the Kubernetes deployment, which enforces the full security model, and to upgrade to 1.3.0-incubating, which documents that the local JVM and single-node Docker Compose deployments do not provide the full security model and should only be used by trusted users.

t: Apache StormCrawler: Server-Side Request Forgery and Cross-Origin Credential Disclosure via robots.txt Redirect Handling
d: Description When StormCrawler fetches a host's `/robots.txt` and receives a redirect, `HttpRobotRulesParser` resolves the `Location` header and re-fetches the target for up to five hops. The loop checks neither the scheme, the host nor the port of the resolved target, and it is not governed by `http.allow.redirects`, which only affects the page fetch. A crawled site can therefore point the robots.txt fetch at any address reachable from the fetcher worker, including loopback interfaces, private ranges and cloud metadata endpoints. Every crawled URL triggers a robots.txt fetch on a cache miss, so no unusual configuration is required to reach the loop. The fetched body is only parsed as robots rules and is not returned to the caller, so the read itself is blind. The more direct impact is on credentials: the okhttp protocol applies its configured request headers, including the `Authorization` header built from `http.basicauth.user` and `http.basicauth.password` and anything in `http.custom.headers`, to every request it makes. Because StormCrawler follows the redirect itself and issues a new request, okhttp's own removal of the `Authorization` header across a host change does not apply, and the operator's crawl credentials are delivered to the host the redirect names. The connection-time IP filter, `http.filter.ipaddress.include` and `http.filter.ipaddress.exclude`, is installed as an okhttp network interceptor on the same client and does apply to these hops when it is configured. It ships with no rules, which is why the path is reachable in a default configuration. URL filtering never applies, because the robots.txt fetch does not pass through the outlink filter chain. Mitigation Upgrade to 4.0.0, where a robots.txt redirect is followed only when the target uses http or https and shares scheme, host and port with the URL it was reached from. Deployments that legitimately serve robots.txt through a cross-host redirect can restore the previous behaviour with `http.robots.redirect.crosshost.allow`. Users who cannot upgrade immediately should set `http.filter.ipaddress.exclude` to cover loopback, private, link-local and CGNAT ranges, which is enforced after DNS resolution and therefore also on redirect hops. Operators who configure `http.basicauth.*` or `http.custom.headers` for a crawl should assume those credentials may have been sent to third-party hosts and rotate them, and should scope credentials by running a separate topology per origin. Credit Independently reported to the Apache StormCrawler PMC by n0mi1k, with a proof of concept. Also found by the ASF -- using Claude agents to study the security of open-source projects, validated and reported by Apache StormCrawler.

t: Apache StormCrawler: Crawled Content Injects Crawler Control Metadata via the SQL Status Store
d: Description The SQL status backend serialises per-URL metadata into a single column by concatenating a tabulation, the key, an equals sign and the value, with no escaping. On read-back the string is split on the same two characters, so the round trip is not injective: a value that contains a tabulation returns as one or more additional keys that were never written. Values on that path are supplied by crawled servers. `FetcherBolt` records the raw `Location` header of a redirect as `_redirTo`, and `_redirTo` is part of the default `metadata.persist` set, so a redirect whose `Location` contains a tabulation followed by `key=value` pairs introduces those keys into the crawler's own control metadata on the next scheduling cycle. Several control keys are read without a prefix, so the injected keys are live: `http.proxy.host`, `http.proxy.port`, `http.proxy.user` and `http.proxy.pass` among them, as well as scheduling and request-shaping keys such as `depth`, `max.depth`, `crawl.delay`, `http.content.limit` and `isSitemap`. Where a proxy manager is configured, the consequence is not limited to corrupted scheduling data. `SingleProxyManager.getProxy(Metadata)` consults the per-URL metadata first and returns what it finds, so an injected proxy host and port take precedence over the operator's configured proxy and subsequent fetches, together with any configured `Authorization` header, are routed through a host the crawled content chose. A related defect in `AbstractStatusUpdaterBolt` compounds this: an injected `status.store.as.is.with.nextfetchdate` that is not a valid instant escapes the enclosing try/catch and stops the bolt, and because the stored row is replayed the failure repeats. Deployments using the OpenSearch or Solr status backends are unaffected, because those serialise metadata structurally. Mitigation Upgrade to 4.0.0, where the metadata column is written in an escaped form behind a format marker, rows written by earlier versions are still decoded unchanged, and the stored next-fetch-date is parsed defensively. The fix does not repair rows written before the upgrade. Operators using the SQL status backend should inspect the metadata column of an existing status table for tabulation characters and remove the affected rows, and should assume any proxy credentials configured for the crawl may have been exercised through an attacker-chosen proxy and rotate them. Users who cannot upgrade immediately can remove `_redirTo` from `metadata.persist` to close the demonstrated path, though other crawled values reaching persisted metadata remain. Credit Independently reported to the Apache StormCrawler PMC by n0mi1k, with a proof of concept. Also found by the ASF -- using Claude agents to study the security of open-source projects, validated and reported by Apache StormCrawler.

t: Multiple Vulnerabilities in GlobalEduca's Job Portal
d: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in 'experiencia_laboral[descripcion]' field in the POST request to '/personas/{persona_id}/experiencias_laborales' on the job portal. The server stores the data entered by an authenticated candidate and displays it in the recruitment interface without sanitizing it. When reviewing an application, the recruiter’s browser can execute the injected JavaScript code within the context of their session on the portal.

t: Apache StormCrawler: Host-Only Cookies Sent to Any Host
d: Description `CookieConverter.getCookies` decides which stored cookies to attach to an outbound request. The applicability check is nested inside a test for the presence of a `Domain` attribute, so a cookie without one, which is the ordinary form of a session cookie, skips scoping entirely and is returned for whatever target URL was passed. RFC 6265 requires the opposite: a cookie with no `Domain` attribute is host-only and belongs to the host that set it. Two further defects sit in the same method. The domain comparison has no notion of a registrable domain, so a `Domain` value of `com` matches every host under it, and the comparison returns true when it throws, so a failure to evaluate the check admits the cookie. Neither the converter nor `MetadataTransfer`, which carries the stored cookie to outlinks, ever considers the host that issued it. Cookie handling is opt-in: it requires `http.use.cookies` to be set to true, which is not the default, and the cookie key to be listed in `metadata.transfer`. The documented recipe does not work as written, because the `metadata.transfer` example in the internals documentation names `set-cookie` while the key present in metadata is `protocol.set-cookie` and the transfer matches key names exactly. Deployments affected are therefore those where an operator determined the correct key, enabled cookie handling and crawls an authenticated site whose pages link or redirect to other hosts. In that case the session cookie of the authenticated origin is sent to those hosts. Mitigation Upgrade to 4.0.0, where a cookie without a `Domain` attribute is sent only to the host that set it, a single-label domain is rejected and the domain check fails closed. Because the protocol does not yet record the host that issued a cookie, cookies without a `Domain` attribute are not sent at all until that host is recorded; operators relying on cookie transfer will notice this. The documentation error is corrected in the same release. Users who cannot upgrade immediately should confine an authenticated crawl to a topology whose URL filters keep it on the origin that issued the credentials, and should not rely on cookie scoping as a boundary. Rotating session credentials used for such crawls is advisable. Credit Independently reported to the Apache StormCrawler PMC by n0mi1k, with a proof of concept. Also found by the ASF -- using Claude agents to study the security of open-source projects, validated and reported by Apache StormCrawler.

t: Apache StormCrawler: HostURLFilter Domain Scoping Silently Disabled by a Wrong Variable Check
d: Description `HostURLFilter.configure` reads the `ignoreOutsideDomain` parameter but tests the node belonging to `ignoreOutsideHost` when deciding whether the domain mode was configured. A filter configuration that names only `ignoreOutsideDomain`, which the class documentation presents as an independent mode, is therefore discarded: the flag is forced to false, `filter` short-circuits on its guard and every URL is returned unchanged. The filter enforces nothing while appearing to be configured, and the failure is silent. The mirror-image configuration, naming only `ignoreOutsideHost`, fails with a `NullPointerException` while the topology is starting. The effect is the loss of a scope control the operator configured, so a crawled page's outlinks are followed to hosts the operator intended to exclude. Impact beyond crawl scope depends on what the crawler then fetches and is not claimed here. Projects generated from the StormCrawler Maven archetypes are not affected, because all three shipped filter configurations set both parameters. Mitigation Upgrade to 4.0.0, where each parameter is tested independently. Operators whose configuration sets only `ignoreOutsideDomain` will find the crawl restricted to the source domain, as configured, which may reduce the number of outlinks accepted. Users who cannot upgrade immediately should set both `ignoreOutsideHost` and `ignoreOutsideDomain` explicitly in the `HostURLFilter` configuration, which produces the intended behaviour on affected versions. Credit Independently reported to the Apache StormCrawler PMC by n0mi1k, with a proof of concept. Also found by the ASF -- using Claude agents to study the security of open-source projects, validated and reported by Apache StormCrawler.

t: Multiple Vulnerabilities in GlobalEduca's Job Portal
d: Uploading PDF files with active content to the languages form. The POST endpoint ‘/people/{person_id}/languages’ checks the declared MIME type and allows an authenticated user to upload a PDF with embedded JavaScript. The portal serves the file via a GET request to ‘/attachments/{attachment_id}’ with the ‘Content-Disposition: inline’ header, so it can be opened in the browser’s PDF viewer during review. The handling of active content depends on the viewer used.

t: SUSE NeuVector DLP/WAF rule inside every documented validation limit overflows a 2048-byte stack buffer in the enforcer dataplane
d: A stack buffer overflow in DLP/WAF in the enforcer dataplane of SUSE NeuVector before 5.5, 5.5 before 5.5.6, 5.6.0 before 5.6.5 could be used by remote attackers to crash or potentially execute code.

t: TypesenseVectorStore doDelete filter injection via document ID allows unintended document deletion
d: TypesenseVectorStore is vulnerable to a document ID injection in its delete operation that can cause unintended documents to be deleted. TypesenseVectorStore.doDelete(List<String>) builds a Typesense filter_by expression by raw string concatenation of caller-supplied document IDs into the form id: [id1,id2,...] . The Typesense id field uses bare (unquoted) values in this list form with no escaping mechanism. An ID containing characters with syntactic meaning in the Typesense filter grammar — such as a comma ( , ), a closing bracket ( ] ), or operator tokens ( || , && ) — can break out of the list literal and alter the structure of the filter expression. An attacker who controls a document ID passed to the delete operation can use this to delete documents other than the intended ones (comma injection), or to construct a filter that matches every document in the collection (operator breakout), resulting in unintended bulk deletion. Applications that pass externally supplied or user-controlled document IDs to VectorStore.delete(List<String>) backed by TypesenseVectorStore are affected.

t: Multiple Vulnerabilities in GlobalEduca's Job Portal
d: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in 'carta_presentacion[contenido]' field in the POST request to '/personas/{persona_id}/cvs/{cv_id}/carta_presentaciones' on the job portal. The server stores the data entered by an authenticated candidate and displays it in the recruitment interface without sanitizing it. When reviewing an application, the recruiter’s browser can execute the injected JavaScript code within the context of their session on the portal.

t: Neuvector scanner writes registry credentials world-readable to a /tmp file
d: The SUSE NeuVector image scanner before version 4.331 writes each per-scan task request to a temporary file on disk with mode 0644 (world-readable). This could allow local attackers to gain the registry access credentials of the scanned images.
A logical flaw vulnerability exists in the ZTE Nubia RedMagic 9S Pro+. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may compromise confidentiality.

Z80 Ultra is affected by an information disclosure vulnerability in service interfaces related to application scenarios. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may result in an impact on confidentiality.

t: An SQL injection vulnerability was found in the ADM Defender of ADM
d: An SQL injection vulnerability exists in the firewall management component of ADM Defender due to insufficient validation and improper handling of input data in SQLite queries. This vulnerability may allow an attacker with access to the affected functionality to manipulate database queries, potentially resulting in unauthorized access to or modification of firewall-related data. Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

t: An improper authorization vulnerability was found in the Wallpaper Component of ADM
d: An improper authorization vulnerability exists in the wallpaper component of ADM. An authenticated, low-privileged user can bypass shared-folder access controls by specifying an image path within a restricted share. The CGI processes the request with root privileges without enforcing the source share's access permissions, allowing the attacker to copy and retrieve images they are not authorized to access, resulting in unauthorized information disclosure. Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.
Z80 Ultra product has an improper access control vulnerability in the game assistant module. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may affect confidentiality and integrity.

t: Multiple Vulnerabilities in GlobalEduca's Job Portal
d: Authorization bypass using a user-controlled token (IDOR) on the GlobalEduca job portal. The GET endpoint ‘/attachments/{attachment_id}’ fails to verify whether the attachment belongs to the authenticated user. A user with a registered account can enumerate sequential identifiers and download attachments belonging to other candidates, including resumes containing personal data.
Z80 Ultra product has an improper modification control vulnerability. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may affect integrity and availability.

t: Unblu Spark: Stored Cross-Site Scripting through Uploaded Files
d: Cross-site scripting in the conversation file-sharing feature of Unblu inc. Unblu Spark 7.0 through 7.57.10 and 8.0 before 8.41.1, on on-premises and cloud deployments, allows an unauthenticated remote attacker in the visitor role to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of a user who opens a crafted link to a file the attacker uploaded, via a file type that the browser renders as active content, such as SVG. The JavaScript runs in the context and under the identity of that user's session. Exploitation requires the victim to open the crafted link.

t: A heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability was found in the Network Settings of ADM
d: A heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the Wi-Fi connection handler of ADM allows an authenticated administrator to corrupt heap memory and terminate the affected CGI request by supplying an oversized Wi-Fi pre-shared key. Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

t: A heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability was found in the Network Settings of ADM
d: Insufficient bounds checks in the Link Aggregation handler of ASUSTOR ADM allow an authenticated administrator to submit an excessive number of interface tokens. Crafted requests can corrupt memory and terminate the affected privileged CGI process. Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

t: A reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability was found in the ADM
d: A reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in the initialization component of ADM. When the NAS is uninitialized, the endpoint accepts an unauthenticated sid query parameter and inserts its URL-decoded value into an inline JavaScript string without proper JavaScript-context encoding. An unauthenticated remote attacker can craft a malicious URL that, when opened by a user, executes arbitrary JavaScript in the ADM management origin. Successful exploitation may allow manipulation of the setup page and execution of same-origin requests in the victim's browser. The vulnerability is limited to the first-run initialization state. Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

t: Operation Delegation SSRF protection bypass via DNS rebinding in Eclipse BaSyx Java Server SDK
d: In Eclipse BaSyx Java Server SDK versions 2.0.0-milestone-10 to 2.0.0-milestone-16, the destination validation of the Operation Delegation feature, introduced to prevent server-side request forgery (CVE-2026-7412), can be bypassed through DNS rebinding. Before dispatching a delegated Operation invocation, the server resolves the host of the `invocationDelegation` qualifier URI and rejects loopback, private, link-local, multicast and cloud metadata addresses. The outbound HTTP client (Reactor Netty), however, performs its own, independent DNS lookup when opening the connection and does not use the validated addresses. An attacker who can create or update a Submodel Operation and controls the DNS records of the delegation host can answer the validation lookup with a public address and the connection lookup with an internal address. No authentication is required when the authorization feature is not enabled. Invoking the Operation then causes the BaSyx server to send HTTP POST requests to destinations the protection is meant to block, such as services in internal IT/OT networks, loopback-only interfaces, or cloud metadata endpoints. The server can be used to pivot into network segments that are not directly reachable by the attacker. Only deployments with the Operation Delegation feature enabled are affected. The feature is enabled by default. The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Java Server SDK 2.0.0-milestone-17.

t: Unblu Spark: Improper Access Control for Conversation Session Resources
d: Missing authentication in the conversation session resource handling of Unblu inc. Unblu Spark 7.0 through 7.57.10 and 8.0 before 8.38.0, on on-premises and cloud deployments, allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to download a resource of a conversation session via its exact URL, without an agent session. The resource URLs contain random identifiers that can't be guessed, so the attacker must obtain the exact URL of a resource first.

t: A cleartext transmission of sensitive information vulnerability was found in the ADM Notifications
d: A cleartext transmission of sensitive information vulnerability in the ADM Notifications allows network eavesdroppers on the outbound network path to obtain Clickatell service credentials via the SMS. When executing an SMS test for Clickatell Communicator Central, the backend function Send_Test_SMS embeds the sensitive contents directly into an unencrypted HTTP request URL. An observer on the NAS network egress path can capture the plain text credentials and message payload since the initial request is transmitted without TLS protection or secret redaction. Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

t: Incomplete Fix for CVE-2026-45756: JsonPath Queries Can Still Hold a Process Through search(), match() and Chained Filters
d: The fix for CVE-2026-45756 lowers pcre.backtrack_limit to 10000 around each preg_match() call of the match() and search() filter functions. That limit applies to one starting position, not to one call. PCRE resets its counter at every position it tries a match from. So an unanchored pattern that stays just under the limit is paid once per byte of the subject. Each call also starts from a fresh limit, so chaining clauses in one filter multiplies the work.
